questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was definitely the city, but also the country in general, as I wanted to improve my german language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think there is a lot, that you need to do before going abroad. KU was very helpfull in answering questions, however I think that HU is very confusing, and from the information received from HU I had misunderstood a lot because it was very confusing with the information that you were given from them. However they were very fast in their response, and they tried to answer questions in their best way possible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, I think you were very much on your own to figure out the different things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I must be honest, but me and my co-erasmus students were very confused when we arrived. Everything ws confusing, and a lot of important information was given in German, which was a barrier for many. Additionally signing for the right courses and figure out how many etc a house was, was also very difficult. Me and some other erasmus student spend MANY hours figuring out the system.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, however I was also lucky, as I borrowed an appartment from some family friends.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That Berlin is a fantastic city! additionally it it nice to have roommates who is german as they can show you other parts of Berlin

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not apply for a student house. However I know that it can be very difficult and expensive to find a room.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very bureaucratic and confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think there is a lot of unspoken procedure, that you as an Erasmus student are not aware of. Everything is in german, which for some also can be very challenging in he beginning, where everything is new.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office was very helpful, however sometimes you as a new student coming from abroad was not aware of what to ask. fx. I missed some deadlines for signing for a course, as I did not know there was a deadline, and it was before my arrival.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not very pleased. I think it was difficult navigating in the system. it was hard to figure out, when you needed to sign in for a class, and when not to sign in for a class. However on the positive note, the professors was very nice.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: try to create your own overview, and maybe find a HU student from you faculty that can be your mento for a day, to secure that you understand everything, and that a person who knows the system from a student perspective can help you out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the level was quit high, and I like it. The university is not very digital, which really was surprising for me.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think a lot of the courses had a challenged level which was nice. However, I had arbitration which was on LLM niveau. That level was to high for me, as I had never had arbitration before, so I found it hard to keep up in that course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different. I am use to get 15 minutes break every hour which I think is really good, so you can take some air. At HU you don't get any breaks between classes. 

HU is very pretty from the outside, however inside it could need some improvement regarding the air, chairs, etc. IN UCPH the teaching is more eletrocnic, there is a good study environment etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Kapitalmarkrecht

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: MEUC was a very nice course. it improve your english, but also teach you to speak in front of a lot of people.

questions.answer: Nothing I think

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going to a restaurant. The food in grocery stores are similar to the pricing in DK due to the inflation, however it is still very cheap to eat a restaurants.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
You can sign up for sports through HU, which was very nice and cheap! 
ps. a good way to meet others.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had some international students events, Sports for all HU students which was really nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the sport! it is very nice, and a good way to meet others.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: goo to the different areas in Berlin. each area has its own city. Go to poland, museums, art galeries, clubbing, markets etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the HU-sports. Try talking to them in class

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: for mere it was more the general system in Germany which is quit different from my home country. It was always very bureaucratic, physical papers, long waiting time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn some basic German before going there. 
ask a lot of questions to the international office before going there. 
Everything will turn out great!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to learn a lot of international students, ,which was very nice. It opened my cultural horizons, improved my language

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: navigating HU system

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
